source: IRS Schedule C (Form 1040) 2025, verified against https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf on 2026-07-28
notes: This is a REFERENCE scheme, not a client chart of accounts. Swap this file to code against any client's own COA. Only 'account', 'auto_assign' and 'confidence_floor' are required per entry; every other field is optional and used only to improve suggestions.

confidence_policy.scored_separately: Score read_confidence and account_confidence independently. read_confidence is how clearly the receipt was read. account_confidence is how sure the account is, given what was read. Routing below uses account_confidence.
confidence_policy.auto_assign_false_rule: An account marked auto_assign: false is not assignable from a receipt. Route to a fallback and report account_confidence below route_to_fallback_below, because confidence in an account you may not assign is zero.
confidence_policy.rule: Never invent an account name that is not in this file. When nothing fits, use a fallback and say why.

always_flag_for_review: receipt total is unreadable or partially obscured
receipt appears to be personal rather than business
vendor matches more than one account with similar confidence
receipt contains both business and personal line items
date is missing or outside the last 24 months
possible duplicate of another receipt in the same batch

fallback_accounts.purpose: Readable receipt, but the correct account is genuinely ambiguous. Needs a human decision.
Receipt could not be read well enough to code at all.

accounts.notes: Costs to promote the business to potential or existing customers.
Actual vehicle costs. If the client uses the standard mileage method instead, fuel and maintenance receipts are NOT separately deductible. Flag for review when the method is unknown.
Payments to non-employees for producing business. Not merchant processing fees, which go to Other Expenses.
Payments to independent contractors. Amounts of 600.00 or more per payee generally require a 1099-NEC. Flag any single payment at or above 600.00 so the 1099 tracking is not missed.
Not a receipt-coded account. Present for completeness only. Never auto-assign from a receipt.
Capital asset purchases. A receipt for a large asset should be flagged to the bookkeeper for a capitalize-versus-expense decision, not auto-coded here.
Benefits other than pension and profit-sharing, which go to line 19.
Business insurance premiums. Owner health insurance is an adjustment on Form 1040, not a Schedule C expense.
Mortgage interest paid to banks on business real property. Comes from a statement, not a receipt.
Business loan and credit card interest.
Attorneys, accountants, bookkeepers, and consultants.
Consumable office costs including postage and shipping. Distinguish from Supplies, which are consumed in producing the service.
Employer plan contributions for employees. Not receipt-driven.

accounts.account: Rent or Lease - Vehicles, Machinery, Equipment
accounts.notes: Short-term equipment and vehicle rentals belong here, not Travel.

accounts.account: Rent or Lease - Other Business Property
accounts.notes: Office, studio, warehouse, and storage. Home office does NOT go here; it is Form 8829 and Schedule C line 30.
Keeps property in working order. An improvement that extends useful life is a capital item, not a repair. Flag when the receipt suggests an improvement.
Materials consumed in the business. Big-box vendors sell across several categories, so a Home Depot or Amazon receipt should be coded from its line items where readable, and flagged when it is not.
Business licenses, permits, and employer payroll taxes. NOT federal income tax, and NOT sales tax paid on a purchase, which stays with the underlying expense.
Overnight business travel away from the tax home. Local commuting is never deductible. Meals while traveling go to line 24b, not here.

Business meals are 50 percent deductible. Entertainment is 0 percent and is not deductible at all. A receipt with a bar tab or event tickets alongside food should be split or flagged. Business purpose and attendees must be recorded; if the receipt does not show them, flag for review.
Mixed-use phone and internet are deductible only at the business-use percentage. Flag any personal-name utility bill for the business-use split.
W-2 employee wages, from payroll reports rather than receipts. Owner draws are never wages on Schedule C.
Section 179D, requires Form 7205. Never auto-assign from a receipt. Present so the scheme matches the current form layout, where 27a is NOT the other-expenses line.
Flows through Part V line 48 to line 27b. Itemized by description on Part V.

accounts.account: Other Expenses - Bank and Merchant Fees
accounts.notes: Flows through Part V line 48 to line 27b.
Country club and social club dues are NOT deductible. Flag those rather than coding them.
Must maintain or improve skills in the current trade. Education qualifying the client for a new trade is not deductible.
Ordinary and necessary, fits no named line, and does not fit the named Part V buckets above. Prefer Ask My Accountant over this when uncertain.
Part III. Goods bought for resale. Only applies to businesses carrying inventory.
Part III. Do not include amounts paid to the owner.
Part III. Materials that become part of the product sold. Distinguish from line 22 Supplies, which are general operating supplies.

counting.rule: When asked how many accounts this scheme has, count the accounts array and report it. Count fallback_accounts separately and say so. Do not estimate and do not rationalize a number after stating it.
